claim: The Alto Valle del Rio Negro was planted with fruit orchards before anyone planted vines.
because: Vines came before the orchards or at the same time, not after. Humberto Canale was founded in 1909 and helped build Patagonian winemaking. Agrarian-history studies of the valley describe the 1910s as an alfalfa economy with small areas of vines and fruit trees, mixed alfalfa/vine/fruit farms, and alfalfa being replaced by vines, pears and apples by the mid-1920s. Apple and pear growing only became the valley's main business around 1930. The bank's own explanation for i-ue88uyhi also says some Rio Negro vines are a century old, which contradicts this sentence.
fix: The Alto Valle del Rio Negro grew vines alongside alfalfa and fruit from the early 1900s, and later became better known for its apple and pear orchards.
